endorsements.quote: Nurses also need practical support to use these tools safely. This includes training in how to interpret uncertainty, recognise possible bias, explain limitations to families and decide when to question or override an automated recommendation.
Artificial intelligence literacy should be embedded in undergraduate nursing education, continuing professional development and organisational training.
Second, health organisations should introduce artificial intelligence into family nursing through staged implementation and evaluation rather than rapid deployment.
Nurses should use artificial intelligence–supported recommendations as prompts for assessment and conversation.
Families should be told when artificial intelligence–supported tools are being used, what the tools can and cannot do, and how to contact a nurse when they need human support.
Second, health organisations should introduce artificial intelligence into family nursing through staged implementation and evaluation rather than rapid deployment.
Policies should require accessible formats, culturally appropriate communication, alternatives to digital‐only support and monitoring of unequal use or outcomes.
Education should also prepare nurses to explain artificial intelligence–supported tools to families in clear, non‐technical language.

unlisted_practices: Require co-design of AI tools with nurses, families, patients, data scientists, ethicists and policymakers, including families with low digital access.
Create payment and reimbursement models for nurse-led, technology-enabled family care such as remote monitoring, digital counselling and post-alert follow-up.
Distinguish locked from adaptive AI systems and require post-implementation monitoring and adverse-event reporting.
Establish family-level data governance including family-level consent for data involving multiple people.
Require usability and acceptability testing of AI tools with nurses and families before routine use.
Avoid digital-only models of family support and preserve human nurse contact.
Inform families when AI is used and give them accessible ways to raise concerns.
Include family-relevant outcomes such as caregiver burden, trust and continuity in AI evaluation, not only efficiency or cost.

screen.reason: The paper synthesizes literature to propose a policy framework and set of recommendations for the safe, equitable, and human-centred integration of AI into family nursing.
